title: How to track customer meetings in your CRM with Google Calendar
summary: Learn how to track customer meetings in your CRM by syncing Google Calendar, so past and upcoming meetings show up on the right deal without manual logging.
body_markdown:
To track customer meetings, use a CRM with Google Calendar integration so events attach to the right deal automatically. Manual logging is the usual method and the usual failure point, because it depends on every rep entering every meeting by hand. A calendar integration removes that step: past and upcoming meetings appear on the deal on their own.


## Why meeting activity belongs in your CRM


A CRM is meant to show the real state of every deal, and meetings are the clearest signal a deal is alive. Yet meetings usually live only in a calendar and never reach the CRM. That creates two gaps:


- **Managers can’t see what’s real.** Reviewing a pipeline, a manager can’t tell which deals have had actual conversations and which have stalled, so forecasts rest on guesswork.
- **Reps lose the thread.** Without upcoming meetings on the deal, reps bounce between calendar and CRM to remember what’s next.


The standard fix — “log every call, write a note after every meeting” — fails because manual entry is tedious and the first habit to slip under load.


## Ways to bring meetings into your CRM


Three approaches are common. They differ mostly in how much ongoing effort they take and how complete the record ends up.


Approach How it works Effort Completeness


Manual logging Reps add each call or meeting and notes by hand High, ongoing Spotty, depends on discipline


Email capture (BCC) Forward or BCC event emails into the CRM Medium Captures email, not meetings


Calendar integration CRM syncs calendar events onto the matching deal None after setup Complete for scheduled meetings


For most teams, a calendar integration is the only one that stays complete without daily effort.


## How Google Calendar sync with a CRM works


A calendar integration reads your calendar and matches each event to a contact or deal already in the CRM. Matched events appear on that record automatically: past meetings as history, upcoming meetings as what’s next. Strong integrations share four traits:


- They pull **events from** **any teammate** with access to the deal, so a manager sees meetings a rep ran.
- They **respect calendar privacy** , hiding events marked private.
- They keep the timeline readable by **suppressing automated invite emails** .
- They log **call recordings and transcripts** in each deal


## What to look for in a CRM with Google Calendar integration


Calendar integrations can vary from CRM to CRM. In order to find one that provides a full information sync and keeps your team's information secure, look for the following features in a calendar sync:


- **Automatic matching** — events attach to the right deal with no manual step.
- **Past and upcoming** — history and what’s next, not just one.
- **Team-wide visibility** — meetings from anyone on the deal, not only your own.
- **Privacy controls** — events marked private stay private.
- **Pipeline-level meeting metrics** — sort and filter every deal by number of meetings and first, last, and next meeting date, so “which deals are moving” is something you sort, not guess.


## How Streak tracks customer meetings


Streak is a CRM that lives inside Gmail, so your inbox, calendar and pipeline are already in one place.


The[Google Calendar integration](https://www.streak.com/google-workspace-crm#google-calendar) shows meetings on the right deal automatically, matched to the contacts you track.


It pulls events from any teammate with pipeline access, respects your calendar visibility settings, and adds Events columns — **Number of events** , **First event date** , **Last event date** , and **Next event date** — so you can sort a whole pipeline by meeting activity. Gemini meeting notes and recordings attached to the calendar event appear with it, so the meeting record stays on the deal.


In practice: open a deal and see every past and upcoming meeting in the timeline, with Gemini notes and recordings attached. From your Calendar, open an event to see related deals and jump right to the box in Streak. Sort a pipeline by **Last event date** to surface deals that have gone quiet, or by **Next event date** to see the week ahead. Meetings appear without manual logging, and it’s available on all plans.


## Frequently asked questions


### How do I sync my CRM with Google Calendar?


Use a CRM with a Google Calendar integration, like Streak. It matches events to your contacts and shows them on the deal automatically, so you don’t log meetings by hand.


### Which CRMs integrate with Google Calendar?


Several[Google Workspace CRM](https://www.streak.com/google-workspace-crm) s include calendar sync, including Streak. Streak attaches meetings to the deal and adds pipeline-level meeting columns; check each tool for whether it covers past and upcoming events and teammates’ calendars.


### Can I see upcoming customer meetings in my CRM?


Yes. A calendar integration shows upcoming meetings on the deal, not just past ones, so you know what’s next without leaving the CRM.


### Does syncing my calendar to my CRM expose private events?


Not if the integration respects your calendar visibility settings. Streak follows them, so events marked private aren’t shown.


### How do I find deals with no recent meetings?


Use a pipeline column that tracks meeting activity. In Streak, sort by the **Last event date** column to surface deals that have gone quiet.
